ai.description: *Boiga westermanni* reaches 1.2 m. It has a greyish-brown body with dark, transverse, white-edged blotches and a distinct, broad, dark-brown vertebral stripe. The head is triangular with a vertical pupil.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Boiga westermanni* is best distinguished by its distinct, dark-bordered vertebral spots and a pale, unpatterned belly, which lacks the heavy dark mottling seen in other *Boiga*.
ai.habitat: *Boiga westermanni* inhabits dry deciduous forests and scrublands across central and peninsular India, typically found at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: *Boiga westermanni* is a strictly nocturnal hunter that remains coiled and motionless among tree branches during the day to blend in with its surroundings.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Boiga westermanni* is oviparous, laying clutches of 4–7 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with hatchlings appearing shortly thereafter.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Boiga westermanni* is found in central and western India, primarily across the Deccan Plateau and parts of the Aravalli Range, typically at low to moderate elevations.
